_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES = the EVEN 0-based indices 2, 4 and 6 — three of them, this being the 40-mark Term-2 paper. ALL EIGHT rendered indices were opened and accounted for, not just the even ones: idx 0 cover (Series ABCD5/5, SET No. 2, Q.P. Code 65/5/2, 'contains 7 printed pages', 'contains 14 questions', 2 hours / 40 marks); idx 1 HINDI General Instructions + Hindi Q1-Q4; idx 2 ENGLISH General Instructions + SECTION A Q1-Q4; idx 3 HINDI Q5-Q10; idx 4 ENGLISH Q5, Q6 + SECTION B Q7-Q10; idx 5 HINDI SECTION C (खण्ड ग) Q11-Q14; idx 6 ENGLISH SECTION C Q11-Q14; idx 7 BLANK apart from the QR code and the '65/5/2 8' footer (measured at 0.079% dark pixels against 2-6% on every content page, and the footer crop read directly). out/2022-65-5-2/contact.png was opened FIRST, per the brief, and settled the language/parity question in one look; it was then confirmed page by page rather than assumed. NO English overflow onto any odd page and NO parity inversion — a CHECKED absence: idx 3 opens directly on the Hindi '5. x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄ यादृच्छिक चर X …' and idx 5 opens directly on the Hindi 'खण्ड ग' heading, so each English->English hand-off jumps its Hindi page cleanly. The alternation is per CHUNK, not per question, and the two languages happen to need exactly one page each per chunk. Question numbers run 1-14 unbroken with every sub-part present. FOLIO/COVER MISMATCH, the same class the brief records for 2026 65/3/1 and 65/5/1 records for this series: the cover says 7 printed pages and the last folio reads 8. INTERNAL CHOICE = FOUR (Q4, Q7, Q9, Q11). Instruction (vi) prints NO count ('There is an internal choice in some questions.'), so this was established by walking the OFFICIAL MARKING SCHEME question by question — it reprints each question block and then both branches under 'Or': Q4 has A4 with an 'Or' between the two answers [ms idx 3], Q7 has A7.(a)/A7.(b) [ms idx 4-5], Q9 has A9 with an 'Or' [ms idx 6], Q11 has A11.(a)/A11.(b) [ms idx 7-8]. Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q8, Q10, Q12, Q13 and Q14 each have a single answer block with no 'Or' — a checked absence, not an assumed one. Q14 is NOT an internal choice: its (a) and (b) are genuine SUB-PARTS of 2 marks each and the scheme marks BOTH (A14.(a) and A14.(b), no 'Or' between them). Cross-check on marks: primary branches 6x2 = 12 in A, 4x3 = 12 in B, 3x4 + 4 (Q14) = 16 in C, total 40, matching the cover and the marking scheme's 'Maximum Marks : 40' — but per the brief that sum is structurally blind to a MISSED alternative, which is why the count rests on the scheme walk. NO MCQs ANYWHERE, confirmed on all three English pages: all 14 questions are free-response, so every row is 'subjective', no row carries options or an 'answer', and the blind MCQ key re-derivation that anchors 2023-2026 cannot run on this paper at all. Decimal points are BASELINE full stops in this question paper — verified on a 4x crop of idx 6: Q13 prints '1%, 1.2%, 2%' with an ordinary period, so it is transcribed '1.2%' and NOT '1{\cdot}2%'. The MARKING SCHEME disagrees with its own paper and prints them RAISED in A13 ('1·2'), the same QP-vs-MS split recorded for 65/5/1 and for 2023 65/5/1; the paper wins. plan.txt IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, exactly as the brief warns. It claims 11 blocks are already covered by 65/5/1 and 3 are new; the MEASURED overlap, judged by comparing every question's CONTENT against data/2022-65-5-1.questions.json, is 14 rows shared and 5 rows NEW. Its number attribution is off throughout — it says 'Q1#1 = 65-5-1 Q1#1' when this paper's Q1 (vector equation of a line) exists nowhere in 65/5/1 and 65/5/1's Q1 is this paper's Q2; it says 'Q6#1 = 65-5-1 Q9#1' when this Q6 is 65/5/1's Q4; and it lists Q8 (the plane) under TRANSCRIBE when Q8 is a verbatim duplicate of 65/5/1 Q9, while naming NONE of the five questions that are genuinely new. THE MEASURED MAP (this paper -> 65/5/1): Q1 NEW · Q2=Q1 · Q3=Q2 · Q4(a)/(b)=Q6(a)/(b) · Q5=Q3 · Q6=Q4 · Q7(a)/(b)=Q10(a)/(b) · Q8=Q9 · Q9(a) NEW · Q9(b) NEW · Q10 NEW · Q11(a)/(b)=Q13(a)/(b) · Q12=Q12 · Q13 NEW · Q14(a)/(b)=Q14(a)/(b). So CBSE reshuffled the shared blocks and swapped out five: the Section-A vector question, both branches of Section-B Q9, the Section-B definite integral (65/5/1 asks ∫₀^{π/4} dx/(1+tan x); this paper asks ∫₀^{π/2} dx/(1+(tan x)^{2/3})) and the Section-C Bayes question (65/5/1's is three job applicants; this paper's is three factory machines). Per the brief's recommended method, every one of the 14 shared rows was READ ON THIS PAPER'S OWN PAGE to confirm it matches, and then the reference file's stem/context text was reused BYTE-FOR-BYTE so the row dedups cleanly at commit rather than shipping a one-character near-duplicate. NO solutions written for any row, per the brief. THREE ITEMS FOR THE NEXT AGENT. (1) Q4(a) carries the SAME CBSE defect as 65/5/1 Q6(a) — its three given probabilities are mutually inconsistent and the official scheme does not notice; verified independently on a 4x crop of THIS paper's idx 2 rather than inherited from the reference. See the _flag on Q4a, and expect the block again in the remaining 65/5 sets. (2) Q8 asks for the equation of a PLANE and is filed on 'The Plane' (Three Dimensional Geometry), the subtopic added to the live axis on 2026-08-19 for exactly this pre-rationalisation corpus; no flag, since the gap it named is resolved. Q8 is the ONLY plane question on this paper — Q1 is a line in space, and Q14 (a)/(b) are both about the two given LINES (shortest distance, then their point of intersection), so neither belongs there. (3) Q10's exponent is 2/3, NOT √2. The well-known form of this question uses √2 and the contact-sheet thumbnail reads that way; a 4x crop of idx 4 shows '(tan x)^{2/3}' unambiguously and the marking scheme's A10 works the whole solution in cos^{2/3}/sin^{2/3}. The answer is π/4 either way, so nothing downstream would have caught a misread. ALSO NOTED, affecting no row: the marking scheme's A12 working prints an incoherent penultimate line, '= 1/2 + [4 − 4/2 − 2 + 1/2]' followed by '= −1 + 2 = 1' — the bracket evaluates to 1/2 and the stated final area 1 is correct, so this is a typesetting slip inside CBSE's own solution, not a question defect. It is the identical slip recorded on 65/5/1, which is unsurprising: Q12 is the same question in both sets.

questions.subtopic: Equation of a Line in Space
questions.stem: Find the vector equation of a line passing through a point with position vector \(2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}\) and parallel to the line joining the points \(-\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + \hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\).

Find the general solution of the following differential equation :

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x-y} + x^2 e^{-y}\)

Events A and B are such that

\(P(A) = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(P(B) = \dfrac{7}{12}\) and \(P\left(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}\)

Find whether the events A and B are independent or not.
questions._flag: CBSE DEFECT — the three given probabilities are MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT. Verified independently on THIS paper (a 4x crop of page idx 2), not inherited from the 65/5/1 transcription: the bars are printed over A and over B SEPARATELY, two bars with a clear gap at the union sign, so the given quantity is \(P(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B})\) and De Morgan gives \(P(A \cap B) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4\) — which exceeds \(P(A) = 1/2\) and is therefore impossible for any pair of events. The official marking scheme for 65/5/2 performs exactly that step (A4 writes \(P(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B}) = P(\overline{A \cap B}) = 1 - P(A \cap B)\), then \(P(A \cap B) = 3/4\)) and does NOT notice the contradiction; it concludes 'not independent' by comparing 3/4 against \(P(A)P(B) = 7/24\). Transcribed exactly as printed. The reading \(P(\overline{A \cup B}) = 1/4\) — a single bar spanning the union — would be consistent (it gives \(P(A \cap B) = 1/3 \ne 7/24\), same verdict), but that is NOT what either document prints and it is not adopted here. This is the same printed block as 65/5/1 Q6(a); the defect is a property of the block, so it should be expected in the remaining sets of this series.

questions.stem: A box \(B_1\) contains 1 white ball and 3 red balls. Another box \(B_2\) contains 2 white balls and 3 red balls. If one ball is drawn at random from each of the boxes \(B_1\) and \(B_2\), then find the probability that the two balls drawn are of the same colour.

Let X be a random variable which assumes values \(x_1\), \(x_2\), \(x_3\), \(x_4\) such that \(2P(X = x_1) = 3P(X = x_2) = P(X = x_3) = 5P(X = x_4)\).

Find the probability distribution of X.

Find the equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes \(\vec{r} \cdot \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) = 10\) and \(\vec{r} \cdot \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}\right) + 4 = 0\) and passing through the point \((-2, 3, 1)\).

Let \(\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}\), \(\vec{b} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}\) and \(\vec{c} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\). If \(\hat{n}\) is a unit vector such that \(\vec{a} \cdot \hat{n} = 0\) and \(\vec{b} \cdot \hat{n} = 0\), then find \(\left|\vec{c} \cdot \hat{n}\right|\).

If \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are unit vectors inclined at an angle \(30^\circ\) to each other, then find the area of the parallelogram with \(\left(\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}\right)\) and \(\left(3\vec{a} + \vec{b}\right)\) as adjacent sides.

Solve the following differential equation :

\(\left(y - \sin^2 x\right) dx + \tan x\, dy = 0\)

Find the general solution of the differential equation :

\(\left(x^3 + y^3\right) dy = x^2 y\, dx\)

questions.subtopic: Area Bounded by a Curve and a Line
questions.stem: Find the area bounded by the curves \(y = |x - 1|\) and \(y = 1\), using integration.

In a factory, machine A produces 30% of total output, machine B produces 25% and the machine C produces the remaining output. The defective items produced by machines A, B and C are 1%, 1.2%, 2% respectively. An item is picked at random from a day's output and found to be defective. Find the probability that it was produced by machine B?
